text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The MP involved in the car crash scandal, Sedat Bucak, denies in television interview that he had any connection with arms and silencers found in the car.
- Famous writer Yasar Kemal's lawyer as well as close friend Zulfu Livaneli deny Kemal seeking political asylum in Sweden.
- Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan says government has enough dollar reserves to keep the Turkish lira from sliding.
- Public dismayed by series of scandals and government's bid to censure the press.
- Conservative opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz's house will be searched today for listening devices.
- Bakers object to maximun price for bread set by government.
- Islamist-led government allegedly gearing up to acquit deputy prime minister Tansu Ciller of corruption charges.
- Leading industrialist Rahmi Koc says his car producer company TOFAS may have to close down its plant because of expected influx of cheap foreign vehicles.
- Yilmaz's house may have been bugged for the last two years, including the period when he was prime minister.
